title: The lesson reading screen, round 2
question: The Tutor belongs to the reading. The roll dealt The Two-Voice Lesson — lock it, or take The Second Pass or The Margin.

options.label: The Two-Voice Lesson
options.lineage: the annotated edition: a second voice answering from beneath the text
options.thesis: The Tutor joins the Lesson as a second voice: ask beside a block and the answer sets beneath it, hairline-ruled and quieter than the Lesson, so the page reads as a dialogue you can re-read.
materials: answers set under the block they answer, in the Tutor's voice
hairline rules and a narrower answer measure
the Course rail marks Lessons with threads
options.viewport: The Lesson reads at the 36rem measure. A hairline 'Ask about this' sits beside the block you are on; the answer streams beneath that block in a quieter voice at a narrower measure and stays when you scroll on. The rail carries the Course and marks every Lesson with a thread; the Exercise and the next handoff close the page.
options.risk: Answers become part of the Lesson, so the authored text is no longer fixed: a long thread bloats the page and makes re-reading harder, and the reading column reflows every time the Tutor speaks.

options.label: The Second Pass
options.lineage: the marked copy: a first read and the read you return to
options.thesis: Read first, ask second. The Lesson stays untouched as the first pass; flagging a passage collects it into a Second Pass where each passage carries your question and the Tutor's answer.
materials: flagging from selection, no panel, no interruption
the Pass as a switched view of the Lesson's own column
the rail marks Lessons that have a Pass
options.viewport: The Lesson reads at the measure, untouched. Selecting a passage raises a quiet flag; the close of the Lesson carries the switch — 'Second pass · 4 passages' — and switching shows the Pass in the same column: each flagged passage quoted, your question, the Tutor's answer, hairline-separated. The rail carries the Course and marks which Lessons have a Pass.
options.risk: Separating asking from the moment of confusion is the point and the price: the learner must flag now and ask later, so a question that was clear in the moment can be stale by the time the Pass opens.

options.label: The Margin
options.lineage: the scholar's margin: the text at the measure, the answer beside it
options.thesis: The Tutor's home is the margin. Select a passage, ask, and the answer stays beside it for the Lesson; the measure never moves, and the margin exists only when the Lesson has something to answer.
materials: anchored answers beside the passage they answer
the margin reserved from the wide viewport's dead space; a sheet below lg
the rail marks Lessons with margins
options.viewport: At wide widths the Lesson keeps the 36rem measure and the margin takes the space between it and the panel edge; selecting a passage raises a hairline bracket and the answer sets beside it, anchored, with the ask line at the margin's foot. Below lg the margin becomes a sheet, and the Lesson behaves the same. The rail carries the Course and marks Lessons that have margins.
options.risk: The margin only exists on wide screens; below lg asking falls back to a sheet, and long answers crowd the space beside the passage they answer.
